sentences.text: Her grandmother died in the February she was twelve and left the house at Ferrel to Mariana's mother and her mother's brother jointly, which is the most ordinary thing in Portugal and the beginning of a great deal of trouble.
The argument was about whether to sell it.
Her uncle was in Lisbon and had two children and a mortgage and wanted it sold, and he was not wrong.
Her mother wanted to keep it and could not have told you exactly for what, and she was not wrong either.
It was a stone house with a leaking roof in a village that has a shop three days a week, and it was worth something to a person from outside and nothing at all to anybody in Ferrel.
Mariana's parents argued about it from March to November.
Not constantly and not loudly.
It is important to describe this accurately because it was not a shouting house.

What it was, from March to November, was a house in which a specific subject was under everything — at dinner, in the car, when the phone went and it was Lisbon, in the silence after her mother came off the phone.
Mariana was twelve and she got very good that year at reading a room from the doorway.
The tells were: whether her mother's phone was face down on the table.
Whether her father said *your brother* or *Zé*.
Whether anybody mentioned the roof.
The roof was the worst one.

The roof was leaking from about the June and everybody knew the roof was leaking, and it could not be discussed, because a roof is either worth fixing or it is not and that is the whole argument wearing a hat.
By September her mother had stopped sleeping properly and her father had started being extremely reasonable, which in that marriage was worse than anything.
By November the house had been empty for nine months with the roof going and nobody had been able to have a conversation that reached the end of itself.
Mariana opened the window on the fourteenth of November.

She did it at about seven in the evening, when her parents were out, in the room at the back that faces the oaks, and she opened it the whole way and put the catch on and went and sat in the kitchen with the door shut and did not go back in.
She had thought about it for nine days.

She would like it on the record that she was not being impulsive and that she knew perfectly well that it was not her house and not her argument and not her decision, and that she did it anyway, at twelve, in November, and that if she could go back she is not certain what she would do.
